label: Build an object
description: Put values together into one object. Every input you wire onto it becomes a key of the same name, so `job: open.id` beside `status: "running"` is `{"job": "...", "status": "running"}`, and the keys come out in the order you wrote them. This is what a route's reply body wants, and what a request body wants on the way out: assembling one used to need a script whose whole job was `return {...}`. Nesting is this node inside this node: wire a `JsonObject`'s `object` onto a key of another. Its keys are required like any other port, so a branch that closed skips this node instead of quietly handing on a half-built object. A part that is genuinely optional is written `key?:`, and then it is left out of the object when nothing arrives rather than set to null, which makes a shape with optional parts one node instead of a branch per combination.

outputs.name: object
outputs.description: The object built from the wired inputs, keyed by input name, in written order. Wire it wherever a body or a payload is wanted; a port declaring a record type accepts it once the shape agrees.
